picks.headline: South Korea’s Komca withdrew plans to register AI-assisted music
picks.excerpt: Komca had announced it would allow ‘AI-assisted’ music to be registered as works so long as a human made a creative contribution to lyrics, composition and arrangement — then pulled the plan.
picks.rationale: Korea's collecting society pulled the one rule that would have let AI-assisted songs be registered — it decides whether a Korean writer's AI-touched track can collect at all.

picks.headline: Universal and Sony sue Suno for a second time, claiming platform’s v6 models are ‘the fruit of the same poisoned tree’
picks.excerpt: The new complaint targets Suno's industry-partnered v6 models. US copyright law sets damages for willful infringement at up to $150,000 per work; 60,202 recordings are cited.
picks.rationale: A second suit aimed squarely at the licensed v6 models — the 'we retrained clean' defence is now being tested, and with it the legal footing of anyone shipping Suno output.

picks.headline: Universal and Warner tell judge ‘new use’ clause in AFM agreement is “clear and unambiguous” and does not apply to their AI deals
picks.excerpt: The American Federation Of Musicians sued Universal and Warner over their AI deals, arguing the majors must share AI money with session players under the Sound Recording Labor Agreement.
picks.rationale: The first fight over whether session players get paid when their recordings feed a label's AI deal — it sets the template for every future AI clause in a musician's contract.

picks.headline: Why This Sound Designer Isn’t Afraid Of Generative AI SFX
picks.excerpt: Sound designer and Dallas Audio Post co-owner René Coronado explains why generative AI sound-effects services don't threaten his craft — and where they actually fit in a post workflow.
picks.rationale: A working post house draws the line between where generated SFX save time and where they fall apart — a practical placement test for tomorrow's session.

picks.headline: Brian May on why he’s changed his mind on AI: “We have to resist. We have to control it very, very seriously and very quickly”
picks.excerpt: The Queen guitarist has reversed his earlier optimism about generative AI in music — and it's why he's gone cold on the idea of a Queen avatar show.
picks.rationale: An early AI optimist among legacy artists flips position and kills a planned avatar show — a signal of where catalogue-holder consent is heading.
